items.title: When the Duden first appeared
items.claim: Konrad Duden's first orthographic dictionary was published in which year?
items.reveal:
Duden's Vollstandiges Orthographisches Worterbuch der deutschen Sprache appeared in Leipzig in 1880.

A standard Orthographische Konferenz in 1901 made it the de facto national reference, a role it has held since.
items.why: Standardisation of writing systems was a late 19th-century project across Europe.

items.title: When the Grimms began publishing
items.claim: The first edition of the Brothers Grimm's Kinder- und Hausmarchen appeared in which year?
items.reveal:
Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm collected tales partly from middle-class informants of Huguenot background, including Dorothea Viehmann.

Later editions softened violence in some tales. Their later Deutsches Worterbuch project was completed only in 1961.
items.why: The 'folk' in folklore is often more bourgeois and literate than the framing implies.

items.title: Kant's three critiques
items.claim: Immanuel Kant published three critiques. Which is correct?

options.text: Of Pure Reason (1781), of Practical Reason (1788), of the Power of Judgement (1790)
Of Logic (1700), of Politics (1750), of Religion (1800)
Of Knowledge (1850), of Art (1900), of Science (1950)

items.reveal:
Kant rarely left Konigsberg, but his work reshaped European philosophy. His 1784 essay 'Was ist Aufklarung?' coined a defining slogan: 'Sapere aude'.

The second edition of the first critique (1787) is the version standardly cited.
items.why: Philosophical revolutions can be carried out at a desk in a provincial city.
